\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مسرت} (masarrat)}{مسرت (masarrat)}]{\ur{مسرت} (masarrat) — delight; joy}

\label{lesson:UR-C441-masarrat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a state of mind, then the Urdu for a mood.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مسرت}}
\textbf{\ur{مسرت}} — \emph{masarrat} — \textquotedblleft{}delight; joy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سالگرہ} \ur{پر} \ur{سارا} \ur{کی} \ur{مسرت} \ur{دیکھ} \ur{کر} \ur{سب} \ur{خوش} \ur{تھے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sālgirah par sārā kī masarrat dekh kar sab khush the.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Everyone was happy to see Sara's delight on her birthday.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مسرت}} (\emph{masarrat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{masarra}, \textquotedblleft{}gladness\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{masarrat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{masarrat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sālgirah par sārā kī masarrat dekh kar sab khush the.} — Everyone was happy to see Sara's delight on her birthday.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a state of mind, then the Urdu for a mood, then say \emph{masarrat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{مسرت} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Delight; joy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لطف} (lutf)}{لطف (lutf)}]{\ur{لطف} (lutf) — enjoyment; pleasure}

\label{lesson:UR-C441-lutf}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a mood, then the Urdu for delight.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لطف}}
\textbf{\ur{لطف}} — \emph{lutf} — \textquotedblleft{}enjoyment; pleasure\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہمیں} \ur{سفر} \ur{میں} \ur{بڑا} \ur{لطف} \ur{آیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hameṅ safar meṅ baṛā lutf āyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We really enjoyed the journey.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لطف}} (\emph{lutf}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{luṭf}, \textquotedblleft{}gentleness, grace\textquotedblright{}; in Urdu it has come to mean the pleasure you take in something.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a mood, then the Urdu for delight, then say \emph{lutf} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{شادمان} (shādmān)}{شادمان (shādmān)}]{\ur{شادمان} (shādmān) — joyful; glad at heart}

\label{lesson:UR-C441-shadman}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for delight, then the Urdu for enjoyment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{شادمان}}
\textbf{\ur{شادمان}} — \emph{shādmān} — \textquotedblleft{}joyful; glad at heart\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{امنگ} (umang)}{امنگ (umang)}]{\ur{امنگ} (umang) — a surge of eagerness; high spirits}

\label{lesson:UR-C441-umang}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for joyful, then the Urdu for brimming over.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{امنگ}}
\textbf{\ur{امنگ}} — \emph{umang} — \textquotedblleft{}a surge of eagerness; high spirits\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{نئے} \ur{سال} \ur{کی} \ur{صبح} \ur{میرے} \ur{دل} \ur{میں} \ur{نئی} \ur{امنگ} \ur{تھی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{naye sāl kī subah mere dil meṅ naī umang thī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
On the first morning of the year my heart was full of fresh eagerness.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{امنگ}} (\emph{umang}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{umaṅg}, \textquotedblleft{}elation\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{únmajjati}, \textquotedblleft{}emerges, comes up\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2110).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{umang}, once more

\end{itemize}
